ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Jesse Owens Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit: shared decision-making for lung cancer screening, same-day low-dose CT showing a suspicious left upper lobe nodule, and tobacco treatment. Concerns: He wants to know quickly and plainly whether the spot on the scan is cancer, and what can be done; He has smoked for 35 years, has failed to stop twice on his own, and worries that stopping now is pointless; No doctor had offered him a lung scan before; he wants the same care anyone else would get, without delay; He wants to keep speaking to young people and to keep walking every morning. [S]

tr.td: Shared decision-making visit for lung cancer screening with a decision aid (benefits, false positives, overdiagnosis, radiation, and the need for yearly scans and for tobacco treatment); he chose to be screened

Low-dose CT of the chest without contrast for lung cancer screening (first screen): solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe; enlarged left hilar lymph node 1.6 cm in short axis; mild centrilobular emphysema in both upper lobes; coronary artery calcification, moderate; Lung-RADS 4X (category 4B with additional features of malignancy)
Chest X-ray, posteroanterior and lateral: the left upper lobe nodule is smaller than on the screening CT; no new opacity, consolidation or ground-glass change; no effusion
Advance care planning conversation, about 25 minutes, with his consent

FDG PET-CT: avid left upper lobe nodule, 2.9 cm (SUVmax 9.8); avid left interlobar (11L) node, 1.6 cm (SUVmax 6.1); no avid mediastinal, supraclavicular or contralateral node; no distant uptake. The infrarenal abdominal aorta measures 2.1 cm
MRI of the brain with contrast: no metastases

Endobronchial ultrasound with systematic needle aspiration of stations 4R, 4L, 7, 10L and 11L under moderate sedation: adenocarcinoma in 11L (TTF-1 positive); 4R, 4L, 7 and 10L negative with adequate lymphocytes; PD-L1 (22C3) tumor proportion score 40 percent; tissue next-generation sequencing (reported in six days, with concordant plasma testing): KRAS G12C mutation, STK11 and KEAP1 wild type; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration

Thoracic multidisciplinary tumor board (thoracic surgery, medical and radiation oncology, pulmonology, radiology, pathology, nurse navigator): resectable cT1c N1 M0 stage IIB adenocarcinoma, no EGFR or ALK alteration; recommends three cycles of nivolumab with platinum doublet chemotherapy, restaging, then lobectomy

Pulmonary function tests: spirometry and DLCO (FEV1 2.71 L, 86 percent predicted; FEV1/FVC 0.73; DLCO 86 percent predicted). Predicted postoperative values after left upper lobectomy (14 of 19 segments remaining): FEV1 63 percent and DLCO 63 percent
Pulmonary rehabilitation as prehabilitation during chemoimmunotherapy: 16 supervised sessions of aerobic and strength training with breathing exercises, twice weekly

Restaging CT of the chest and upper abdomen with contrast after three cycles: left upper lobe nodule 1.3 cm (from 2.9 cm); left interlobar node 0.8 cm (from 1.6 cm); no new nodule, node, effusion or ground-glass change; no liver or adrenal lesion

Video-assisted thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal (stations 4L, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9) and hilar lymph node dissection; three days in hospital without complications. Pathology: ypT1a N0 (0 of 16 nodes; treatment effect without viable tumor in the 11L node), 0.7 cm residual adenocarcinoma with 6 percent viable tumor (major pathologic response), margins clear (R0)
Pulmonary rehabilitation after lobectomy: a 12-week program, twice weekly, started

list.item: Solid, spiculated 2.9 cm nodule in the left upper lobe with an enlarged (1.6 cm) left hilar lymph node on today's low-dose screening CT, Lung-RADS 4X (very suspicious); no symptoms of lung cancer. PET-CT, tissue diagnosis and thoracic oncology review booked: resolved, confirmed [S]

Adenocarcinoma of the left upper lobe of the lung, cT1c N1 M0, stage IIB (AJCC 8th edition), resectable: 2.9 cm primary with a positive left interlobar (11L) node on EBUS; mediastinal nodes 4R, 4L and 7 negative; no metastases on PET-CT or brain MRI. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 40 percent (22C3); KRAS G12C mutation; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK or HER2 alteration: active, confirmed [S]

Nicotine dependence, cigarettes: a pack a day for 35 years (35 pack-years); smokes his first cigarette within 30 minutes of waking; two attempts to stop, each lasting a few weeks without medicine: resolved, confirmed [S]

Acute viral upper respiratory infection (rhinovirus on a respiratory panel) on day 13 of cycle 2 of chemoimmunotherapy: runny nose, sore throat and a dry cough for three days, no hypoxia, clear chest X-ray; immune-related pneumonitis and pneumonia excluded; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

After thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with mediastinal and hilar lymph node dissection: ypT1a N0 (0 of 16 nodes), R0, major pathologic response (6 percent residual viable tumor): active, confirmed [S]
Nicotine dependence, cigarettes, in early remission: no cigarettes since day 1 of cycle 1, about four months, on varenicline: active, confirmed [S]

list.item: Smokes a pack of cigarettes a day and has for about 35 years (35 pack-years); no cigars, vaping or cannabis. Has tried to stop twice on his own. Thinks the morning cough is just a smoker's cough [S]
Retired track athlete who runs a small public relations business from home and speaks at schools, youth clubs and corporate events, often travelling; walks 3 km most mornings before the heat [S]
Married; lives with his wife in a suburb of Phoenix, Arizona; three adult daughters live out of state. No relative is named or given a role in his care [S]

Grew up poor in Alabama and Cleveland and met open racial exclusion at university and after the Olympics; has had money worries for much of his life and is careful about costs; Medicare with a supplemental plan [S]
No clinician has ever talked to him about lung cancer screening; his last clinic checked his blood pressure and did a colonoscopy four years ago [S]
Alcohol: a beer or a glass of wine once or twice a week (AUDIT-C 2); no other drug use. No known asbestos, radon or silica exposure [S]

tr.td: New patient visit: shared decision-making for lung cancer screening, same-day low-dose CT showing a suspicious left upper lobe nodule, and tobacco treatment
Diagnosis of left upper lobe adenocarcinoma, stage IIB: thoracic oncology consultation, tumor board plan for chemoimmunotherapy before surgery, and start of varenicline
Day 1 of cycle 2 of nivolumab with carboplatin and pemetrexed: toxicity, immune-related adverse event monitoring, smoking abstinence and prehabilitation
After three cycles: restaging CT, decision for lobectomy, thyroid result and surgical preparation
Six weeks after left upper lobectomy: pathology, surveillance plan, tobacco remission and pulmonary rehabilitation
Same-day sick visit for a cold during chemoimmunotherapy
Referral to thoracic oncology: consultation within two weeks to review the screening CT, PET-CT and EBUS results with him and plan treatment

Work-up of the Lung-RADS 4X nodule without delay: FDG PET-CT and brain MRI with contrast this week, then endobronchial ultrasound with systematic sampling of mediastinal and hilar nodes (at least stations 4R, 4L and 7, and any PET-avid node), with enough tissue for PD-L1 and comprehensive next-generation sequencing (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, KRAS, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK, HER2) and plasma testing in parallel; nurse navigator to track each date
Tobacco treatment at every visit: brief advice, varenicline offered with a quit date, the Arizona quitline and counseling; stopping smoking improves outcomes even after a lung cancer diagnosis
Equity safeguards: a nurse navigator, written results and next steps at each visit, transport and cost help offered, and time from scan to treatment tracked against the goal
Distress and depression screening at each visit, plain information he can share, and advance care planning when he is ready

Chemoimmunotherapy before surgery: nivolumab 360 mg with carboplatin (AUC 5) and pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 every three weeks for three cycles, with folic acid, vitamin B12 and dexamethasone premedication, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests first, and restaging CT before surgery

Immune-related adverse event monitoring: TSH, free T4, liver tests, creatinine, glucose and blood count before each cycle, morning cortisol at baseline and before surgery, and a written list of warning symptoms with a 24-hour oncology line
Physiologic evaluation for lobectomy (spirometry and DLCO with predicted postoperative values) and prehabilitation: a pulmonary rehabilitation program during chemotherapy
Thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with systematic mediastinal and hilar lymph node dissection after restaging shows response and no new disease

After surgery: no further systemic therapy after a major pathologic response, by shared decision; history, examination and chest CT every six months for two to three years, then yearly low-dose CT; pulmonary rehabilitation after surgery; the KRAS G12C result kept on file for any recurrence
PET-CT, brain MRI, EBUS staging, tissue diagnosis, PD-L1 and comprehensive biomarker results and a tumor board plan within three weeks of the screening CT
PET-CT in three days, brain MRI in four, EBUS in eight, tumor board in ten; PD-L1 and tissue sequencing back by the consultation, 15 days after the scan
Stop smoking completely before treatment starts and stay stopped
No cigarettes since day 1 of cycle 1, about four months; varenicline continued to complete 24 weeks
Three cycles of chemoimmunotherapy before surgery without a delay of more than one week and without an immune-related adverse event of grade 2 or higher
Three cycles on schedule; only a grade 1 rise in TSH, monitored without treatment
Complete resection (R0) with systematic lymph node dissection within six weeks of the last cycle
Thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy five weeks after cycle 3; R0; major pathologic response
Back to walking 3 km most mornings by three months after surgery
Walking 2 km a day six weeks after surgery and starting pulmonary rehabilitation

list.item: Fully active and independent (ECOG performance status 0); walks 3 km briskly on the level and climbs three flights of stairs without stopping [S]
Alert, warm and courteous; worried about what the scan could mean; PHQ-2 1; no thoughts of self-harm [S]
